key_insight: A fault-tolerant quantum algorithm can compute open-system battery observables like voltage and differential capacity by embedding strongly coupled electron-lattice and reservoir dynamics into a unitary, chain-mapped Caldeira-Leggett simulation.
engineering_relevance: This enables chemically realistic quantum simulation of cathode lithiation regimes where closed-system methods fail, with direct relevance to battery materials design and validation against experimental voltage plateaus.
method: Unitary chain-mapped Caldeira-Leggett embedding makes bath dynamics Trotterizable.
Fourth-order Trotterization yields polynomial T-gate scaling for open-system evolution.
Calibrated against HEOM in the strong-coupling regime and Lindblad in the weak-coupling limit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with experiment for LiFePO4 within ±5 mV and a LiMn2O4 two-plateau split of 125 mV versus the observed 150 mV, alongside a resource estimate of ~368 logical qubits and ~3×10^5 T-gates per step.
watch_item: The approach is fault-tolerant but still resource-intensive, so full-scale voltage-curve runs require very large T-gate counts and substantial hardware progress.
paper_title: Quantum Algorithm for Open-System Battery Cathodes by Modeling Multiple Strongly Coupled Holstein Polarons with Chain-Mapped Caldeira-Leggett Dynamics
